tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

tools.name: NotebookEdit
tools.description:
Replaces, inserts, or deletes a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file).

Usage:
- You must use the Read tool on the notebook in this conversation before editing — this tool will fail otherwise.
- `notebook_path` must be an absolute path.
- `cell_id` is the `id` attribute shown in the Read tool's `<cell id="...">` output. It is required for `replace` and `delete`.
- `edit_mode` defaults to `replace`. Use `insert` to add a new cell after the cell with the given `cell_id` (or at the beginning of the notebook if `cell_id` is omitted) — `cell_type` is required when inserting. Use `delete` to remove the cell.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

## deepwiki
DeepWiki MCP provides AI-powered documentation for GitHub repositories.

With a user OAuth token, all devin_* tools act in one organization: without an X-Org-Id header, the first one the user joined. Not found usually means another of their orgs; send X-Org-Id: <org id> to switch.

Available tools:
- read_wiki_structure: Get a list of documentation topics for a repository
- read_wiki_contents: View full documentation about a repository
- ask_wiki_question: Ask any question about a repository's codebase and get an AI-powered answer from its wiki
- list_wiki_repos: List the repositories that have a DeepWiki index (private mode only)
- generate_wiki: Generate a codebase wiki for a repository — only use when explicitly requested by the user (private mode only)
- devin_automation_manage: Manage Devin automations — list, get, create, update, delete, or fetch the trigger event schemas (private mode only)
- devin_billing_tag_manage: Manage Devin billing tags (groupings of Devin sessions for usage tracking) — list, get, create, assign sessions, look up session tags (private mode only)
- devin_blueprint_test: Test a candidate blueprint YAML in an authoring VM: start → run initialize → fix → run initialize again (clean VM) → run maintenance → then persist with update_environment_config (private mode only)
- devin_campaign_manage: Read and publish a bot's campaign documents (plan, readings, status) — get, update, validate (private mode only)
- devin_code_scan_manage: Manage Devin code scans, sometimes referred to as 'security scans' or 'Devin Security Swarm' — list scans, list findings, list profiles, get a profile, create a scan, remediate a finding (private mode only)
- devin_knowledge_manage: Manage Devin knowledge notes and suggestions — list, search, get, create, update, delete notes, view folder structure, list/view/dismiss knowledge suggestions (private mode only)
- devin_mcp_server_manage: Manage org MCP server installations — install (marketplace or custom), update, enable, disable, delete (private mode only)
- devin_oncall_manage: Devin Oncall operations — create and manage Oncall responders (alert, bug report and support request triage), get an Oncall report's current responder membership, page through a responder's open issues, and ingest a dashboard into Oncall knowledge (private mode only)
- devin_playbook_manage: Manage Devin playbooks — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_review_manage: Trigger a Devin Review for a pull request, fetch the latest review status, or fetch a completed review's findings (private mode only)
- devin_schedule_manage: Manage scheduled Devin sessions — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_session_create: Create one or more child Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_interact: Manage a Devin session — get status (one or many sessions, optionally with a short AI summary of each), send messages, sleep/terminate/archive/unarchive, read messages & attachments, manage tags (private mode only)
- devin_session_events: Inspect session events — list summaries, fetch full details, or search event contents (private mode only)
- devin_session_search: Search and filter Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_insights: Per-session cost, message counts and AI analysis (issues, action items, classification) — list, get, generate (private mode only)
- devin_user_list: List the organization's users by membership kind (direct members or IdP-group members) (private mode only)
- devin_list_integrations: List all native integrations and MCP servers with their status and settings URLs (private mode only)
- devin_find_setting: Find Devin webapp settings pages and deep-link URLs for them (private mode only)

The Windows lane is the regression fence for filesystem-identifier bugs (issues #7/#8). The only adjustable variable is `DSH_HARNESS_TAG`; when certification advances the tag, update the workflow env and this document together with the DSH peer ranges, and `npm run check:versions` refuses a mismatch.
 
+Both lanes report, but neither gates: `master` carries no required status checks, no rulesets, and `enforce_admins` is off, so a green run does not block a merge and nothing server-side refuses a red one. A green workflow is evidence, never permission — whether a change waits for CI is still a matter of discipline.

# Team performance evaluation

English | [中文](team-performance.zh.md)

## Purpose

The Team performance suite measures the costs that a human or Member can observe across loading, tool calls, ledger reads, Session work, and collaboration. It is an evaluation tool, not a production code path, and it runs only when explicitly enabled.

The source of the scenarios is [`scripts/team-performance/`](../../scripts/team-performance/). The script index lists the entry points and their output formats in [`scripts/README.md`](../../scripts/README.md).

## Run the evaluation

### Baseline

Run the default 16 scenarios in one Node process:

```sh
DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team
```

The command writes a run directory under `artifacts/team-perf/runs/` containing `manifest.json`, measured `samples.jsonl`, and `summary.json`. The default configuration uses three measured samples and one warmup. Use `DSH_BENCH_SCENARIOS` to select scenarios and the matching variables such as `DSH_BENCH_THREADS`, `DSH_BENCH_FOLLOWERS`, `DSH_BENCH_MEMBERS`, and `DSH_BENCH_SESSION_EVENTS` to change workload size.

### Scale matrix

Run the default 15 cases in separate Node processes:

```sh
npm run bench:team:matrix
```

Set `DSH_BENCH_MATRIX_CASES` to a comma-separated list of `scenario:threads:followers`. The matrix routes the first size to Member or Session workloads when the scenario requires it. Each matrix directory contains a manifest, each child run, and an aggregated `results.json`.

### Browser loading

Measure the assembled Web bundle and Team mode:

```sh
DSH_BENCH_BROWSER_SAMPLES=3 npm run bench:team:browser
```

Each sample uses a fresh temporary Web scaffold and Chromium. The runner records page load, Workspace connection, ordinary ready, Team mode ready, navigation timing, transfer bytes, console warnings, and page errors. It writes `manifest.json`, `samples.jsonl`, and `summary.json` under `artifacts/team-perf/browser/runs/`. Browser results must be read with p95 and p99 and with the individual samples because cold startup variance is material.

### Semantic probes

Check the ordered post-commit notification queue:

```sh
DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team:semantics
```

The probe checks failed delivery retry, per-Member ordering, Client invalidation before notification drain, shutdown cancellation, and disposal errors. A passing timing run does not replace these checks.

### Compare runs

Compare two baseline summaries or two matrix result files:

```sh
npm run bench:team:compare -- before/summary.json after/summary.json
npm run bench:team:compare -- --max-regression 20 before/summary.json after/summary.json
```

The comparator reports shared p50, p95, and p99 rows and separately reports missing scenarios and metrics. A regression threshold is meaningful only when the workload, environment, and scenario schema match.

## What the scenarios measure

| Area | Scenarios | Main evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loading and activation | `bundle-size`, `host-boot`, `member-activation`, `member-activation-batch`, `member-resume` | bundle bytes, Host fixture boot, new and resumed Member activation, sequential versus concurrent activation |
| Tool paths | `tool-call`, `tool-read-sweep`, `thread-read-reply`, `tool-write`, `notification-retry` | tool total, Host handler time, result bytes, read/reply and failed-delivery recovery |
| Collaboration | `collaboration-fanout`, `collaboration-agent-turn` | durable commit, Ledger queue wait/service, fan-out dispatch, event-loop lag, notification drain, model request and idle stages |
| Session and storage | `session-fold`, `session-replay-jsonl`, `ledger-read-memory`, `ledger-replay-sqlite` | cursor and projection fold, JSONL write/read/bytes, bounded ledger reads, SQLite open/replay/validation |

The baseline uses real Team Host fixtures and deterministic model adapters where a model turn is needed. It does not claim to represent a production model provider or a live user's machine. The browser scenario is the assembled-path check; the Node scenarios explain the cost inside that path.

## Current constraints

- Notification read material is reused only during one delivery attempt. Facts, delivery plans, and projections are not long-lived caches or a second authority.
- A commit affecting at least eight Members queues notification effects after the durable commit and Client invalidation. Effects remain ordered per Member and are scheduled independently across Members. Effects that have not started when shutdown begins are skipped; the next activation derives the durable unread facts again.
- JSONL `zstd` remains the production default. Uncompressed replay is faster in the measured fixture but uses substantially more disk space.
- Concurrent calls already improve the measured batch Member activation path. The result alone does not justify changing Host startup ordering without a separate startup-restoration experiment.
- Browser cold-start results have a long tail. Keep the sample records and compare distributions; do not turn one run into a hard acceptance threshold.

## Change workflow

When changing a performance-sensitive path, run the narrowest scenario that can observe the change, then run the related scale cases and semantic probes. Compare the same scenario before and after the change. Inspect operation counts and result shape together with wall-clock values; a lower time with missing facts is a failed run. Run `npm test` and `npm run check:artifact` before treating the result as delivered.

Do not place secrets, real profiles, or temporary browser overlays in the repository. The benchmark is opt-in, so ordinary development and release checks do not run it.

2	import type { AgentTeamInboxItem, AgentTeamInboxReminder, AgentTeamMainTimelineEntry } from './types/requests-results.ts'
3	
4	/**
5	 * Every unread fact interrupts: there is one delivery class. An ordinary Thread
6	 * update reaches a reader only because it follows that Thread, a mention or a
7	 * reply carries a direct marker, and a responsibility Activity or live Task
8	 * reminder arrives through its own marker — so what decides whether ordinary
9	 * work exists at all is Attention, never how fast it travels. No identity
10	 * chooses a slower class here. `covered` is what keeps an unchanged
11	 * rederivation from spending a second attempt on the same durable facts.
12	 */
13	export type InboxDelivery = 'immediate'
14	
15	/** The reader's role in one notice scope, as the notice states it. */
16	export type InboxScopeRole = 'follower' | 'member'
17	
18	export interface InboxThreadUnread {
19	  readonly item: AgentTeamInboxItem
20	  readonly facts: readonly AgentTeamThreadReadFact[]
21	  readonly reminders?: readonly AgentTeamInboxReminder[]
22	}
23	
24	export interface InboxMainUnread {
25	  readonly projectRef: AgentTeamProjectRef
26	  readonly entries: readonly AgentTeamMainTimelineEntry[]
27	}
28	
29	export interface InboxDeliveryInput {
30	  readonly threads: readonly InboxThreadUnread[]
31	  readonly main: readonly InboxMainUnread[]
32	  /** Signature of the immediate facts the last delivery attempt answered. */
33	  readonly covered: string | undefined
34	  /**
35	   * Threads the last notice could not render, so its facts were never delivered.
36	   * Their facts still enter this signature — otherwise an unchanged
37	   * rederivation would look identical to the delivered one — but the facts the
38	   * last attempt actually answered are the ones `covered` may match.
39	   */
40	  readonly undelivered?: readonly AgentTeamThreadRef[] | undefined
41	}
42	
43	export interface InboxThreadPlan {
44	  readonly threadRef: AgentTeamThreadRef
45	  readonly role: InboxScopeRole
46	  readonly delivery: InboxDelivery
47	}
48	
49	export interface InboxDeliveryPlan {
50	  /** Why a notice goes out now, or `undefined` when nothing may interrupt the reader. */
51	  readonly trigger: InboxDelivery | undefined
52	  readonly signature: string
53	  /** The signature the next rederivation compares `covered` against: everything the notice can actually render. */
54	  readonly delivered: string
55	  readonly threads: readonly InboxThreadPlan[]
56	}
57	
58	export function planInboxDelivery(input: InboxDeliveryInput): InboxDeliveryPlan {
59	  const immediate: (string | number)[][] = []
60	  const delivered: (string | number)[][] = []
61	  const threads: InboxThreadPlan[] = []
62	  const undelivered = new Set(input.undelivered ?? [])
63	  for (const { item, facts, reminders = [] } of input.threads) {
64	    const threadRef = item.thread.threadRef
65	    // A reminder is always delivered: it is the whole reason the notice exists
66	    // when the Thread holds no ordinary unread.
67	    if (reminders.length > 0) {
68	      const reminderFacts = [threadRef, 'reminder', ...reminders.map(reminder => `${reminder.kind}:${reminder.baselineSequence}`)]
69	      immediate.push(reminderFacts)
70	      delivered.push(reminderFacts)
71	    }
72	    const now = facts.map(entry => entry.fact.sequence)
73	    if (now.length > 0) immediate.push([threadRef, ...now])
74	    // A Thread the notice cannot render is not delivered by this attempt, so its
75	    // facts are not what `covered` records: an unchanged rederivation still sees
76	    // them as owed and re-attempts instead of standing down.
77	    if (now.length > 0 && !undelivered.has(threadRef)) delivered.push([threadRef, ...now])
78	    threads.push(Object.freeze({ threadRef, role: item.attention === undefined ? 'member' : 'follower', delivery: 'immediate' as const }))
79	  }
80	  for (const { projectRef, entries } of input.main) {
81	    if (entries.length > 0) { immediate.push([projectRef, ...entries.map(entry => entry.sequence)]); delivered.push([projectRef, ...entries.map(entry => entry.sequence)]) }
82	  }
83	  const signature = immediate.length === 0 ? '' : JSON.stringify(immediate)
84	  const covered = delivered.length === 0 ? '' : JSON.stringify(delivered)
85	  const trigger = signature !== '' && covered !== input.covered ? 'immediate' : undefined
86	  return Object.freeze({ trigger, signature, delivered: covered, threads: Object.freeze(threads) })
87	}

## Review-state caveats (read first)

**Committed vs uncommitted in the reviewed range (`d39ec06..HEAD` + working tree):**

The ledger-side read-set work (ticket 02 items 2 and 4) therefore exists **only** in the version of the file I captured in `git diff` at the start of this review, not in the tree now. I read that diff before the revert and cite it below.

**Check timeline (per coordinator request):**
- **Before 15:39 (unreliable? no — these ran on the intended tree):** targeted vitest run at 15:37:41 (8 files / 150 passed) — this was before the 15:39:12 ledger revert, so ledger.ts still carried the read-set code; valid for the intended design. `check:boundaries` and `check:docs` ran ~15:37–15:38 (both OK); neither depends on the reverted code.

---

## Findings

### F1 — Deferred notification path swallows invariant divergences (contract violation)
- **Severity:** medium
- **Location:** `packages/agent-team/src/index.ts:2737-2747` (deferred branch) vs `:2758-2763` (synchronous branch); doc contract at `:2729-2733`.
- **Evidence:** The synchronous `afterCommit` re-raises `AgentTeamInvariantError` (`if (error instanceof AgentTeamInvariantError) throw error`, :2761). The new deferred branch catches **every** error and logs it: `catch (error) { this.ctx.logger.warn('agent-team: post-commit ${label} failed: …') }` (:2742-2743). `deliverInboxNotice` deliberately re-raises `AgentTeamInvariantError` (:2932), and it is reached through `notifyMember` from the deferred effect.
- **Impact:** For any commit affecting ≥8 Members (`NOTIFICATION_QUEUE_THRESHOLD`, :194), an integrity divergence inside the notification effect is folded into an ordinary warn instead of staying loud. This contradicts the method's own contract comment ("An invariant divergence is the exception: it is re-raised on the caller's frame so a failed integrity check stays loud") and weakens ticket 02 criterion 2/3 ("wake、recovery、generation swap、通知派生失败和 steer 失败的行为保持现有隔离语义").
- **Basis:** ticket 02 unchecked item "wake、recovery、generation swap、通知派生失败和 steer 失败的行为保持现有隔离语义"; spec "失败隔离逐项一致".
- **Fix:** In the deferred branch, do not fold `AgentTeamInvariantError` into the generic warn — surface it distinctly (e.g. `this.ctx.logger.error` naming the invariant, or a dedicated handler). Async propagation cannot reach the caller frame, so record the divergence at a level that is not silent.

### F2 — Ticket 01's clean-commit criterion genuinely unmet, and the matrix manifest cannot prove it
- **Severity:** medium
- **Location:** `scripts/team-performance/run-team-performance-matrix.mjs:25-28`; `scripts/team-performance/team-performance-baseline.ts:908-911`.
- **Evidence:** All 182 run manifests under `artifacts/team-perf/runs/*/manifest.json` report `dirty: true`; the baseline records `commits` + `dirty` + `status`, but the **matrix** manifest records only `runId, startedAt, samples, warmups, cases, node` — no commit, no dirty flag. So the minimal-matrix artifact carries no clean-tree evidence at all.
- **Impact:** Ticket 01's one open item ("在 clean commit 上跑通最小矩阵，并保留复跑命令和限制") is not satisfied, and cannot be satisfied by the matrix runner as written because it never records the tree state.
- **Basis:** ticket 01 `- [ ] 在 clean commit 上跑通最小矩阵，并保留复跑命令和限制；当前验证工作树包含其他未提交修改`.
- **Fix:** Have the matrix manifest record `teamCommit`, `harnessCommit`, and `dirty` (mirroring the baseline), then rerun the default 15-case matrix on a clean commit and store it.

### F3 — Ticket 02's "逐项一致" criterion is not verified by any probe
- **Severity:** medium
- **Location:** `scripts/team-performance/team-performance-semantics.ts:152-172`; `packages/agent-team/tests/inbox-delivery.spec.ts`.
- **Evidence:** The semantics runner asserts exactly five checks — failure retry, shutdown-not-throw, shutdown-skips-queued, ordering, client invalidation. It never compares notice text / covered / undelivered / attempt / steer-followup ordering against the old path. `inbox-delivery.spec.ts` tests the pure `planInboxDelivery` function only. The read-set change is *equivalent by construction* — `notificationText` receives the plan and falls back to recomputing it from the same inputs (`plan ?? (readerId === undefined ? undefined : this.inboxDeliveryPlan(notifications, main))`, index.ts:3042), and `deliverInboxNotice` still picks `sequenced ? followup : steer` unchanged (:2928-2929) — but no test proves the item-by-item identity the criterion demands.
- **Impact:** Criterion "notice text、covered、undelivered、attempt 和 steer/followup 顺序与旧路径逐项一致" stays unverified; a future regression in the reused plan would not be caught.
- **Basis:** ticket 02 `- [ ] notice text、covered、undelivered、attempt 和 steer/followup 顺序与旧路径逐项一致`; spec seam "旧路径与新路径的 notice text、covered、undelivered、attempt、steer/followup 次序和失败隔离逐项一致".
- **Fix:** Add a probe (or a golden test) that renders a notice through both the plan-passed and plan-recomputed paths over the same facts and asserts identical `text`, `undelivered`, and the recorded `covered`/`attempt`.

### F4 — Ticket 02's isolation criterion is only partially probed (generation swap / steer failure absent)
- **Severity:** medium
- **Location:** `scripts/team-performance/team-performance-semantics.ts` (whole file); probe coverage.
- **Evidence:** The listed subjects include "generation swap" and "steer 失败"; the probe file exercises a forced wake failure on the first call and a shutdown race, but never a generation swap (`retireMemberGeneration`/`activateMember`) or a `steer`-throw isolation path (the failure probe throws from the overridden `steer`, which is the same seam — but there is no swap-generation case). Compounded by F1.
- **Impact:** The unchecked isolation criterion remains open.
- **Basis:** ticket 02 `- [ ] wake、recovery、generation swap、通知派生失败和 steer 失败的行为保持现有隔离语义`.
- **Fix:** Add a probe that drives a Session swap mid-wake and asserts the successor rederives (no duplicate/lost notice), plus an explicit assertion that an invariant divergence from the deferred path is not swallowed (ties to F1).

### F5 — Ordered post-commit notification queue is beyond ticket 02's stated build (scope note, not an excluded item)
- **Severity:** low
- **Location:** `packages/agent-team/src/index.ts:194` (`NOTIFICATION_QUEUE_THRESHOLD = 8`), `:2686-2697`, `:2734-2757`.
- **Evidence:** Ticket 02's "What to build" is "合并单次通知投递的重复派生" (deduplicate per-delivery derivation). The change additionally defers notification effects for ≥8 affected Members into a per-Member ordered, cross-Member parallel queue after commit. The spec's exclusion list ("跨 commit debounce、长期 read-set 缓存、通知上限调整、Member 激活并行和 Session fold 增量") does **not** name this queue, so it is not a listed prohibition, but it is new delivery-timing/parallelism behavior in a slice that asked only to remove duplicate derivation.
- **Impact:** The reviewed uncommitted change is larger than tickets 01–03 describe; the extra behavior is documented in the README and covered by four of the five semantic probes, so it is transparent, but it exceeds the ticket scope.
- **Basis:** ticket 02 "What to build"; spec "第一阶段按三条垂直切片推进 … 2. 把一次通知投递所需的 Thread/Main unread、delivery plan 和文本输入收敛成一次性只读派生结果".
- **Fix:** Either fold this into ticket 02's description explicitly, or split the queue into its own ticket with the F1 invariant behavior fixed.

### F6 — Acceptance seams for tool-call and collaboration are only partly instrumented
- **Severity:** low
- **Location:** `scripts/team-performance/team-performance-baseline.ts:273-345` (tool), `:512-576` (collaboration-agent-turn).
- **Evidence:** Spec seams list startup including **Session inventory**, tool-call including **queue wait / result render / Session write**, and collaboration including **B notice claimed, B read, B reply committed**. Measured: `host-boot` (total only, `mode: 'process-reused'`), `tool-call` (`toolTotalMs`, `hostViewMs` only), `collaboration-agent-turn` (`triggerCommitMs`, `triggerToNoticeQueuedMs`, `noticeQueuedToModelRequestMs`, `modelRequestToAgentIdleMs`, plus warm mirrors). No Session-inventory metric, no per-tool queue-wait/render/Session-write stages, no B-claimed / B-read / B-reply-committed stages.
- **Impact:** The declared acceptance seams are partially covered; the ticket checkboxes are honest about `queue/Session/Agent/Client = null`, but the seam list itself is not fully met.
- **Basis:** spec 验收 seam bullets "启动：storage open、ledger replay/validate、Session inventory、Member activation、Host ready" and "Tool call：… queue wait、ledger/query、结果 render 和 Session 写入" and "协作：A commit ack、B notice queued、B notice claimed、B read、B reply committed、B idle".
- **Fix:** Either instrument the missing stages, or narrow the seam list in the spec to what is actually measured.

### F7 — Doc states a production default it cannot substantiate from this repo
- **Severity:** low
- **Location:** `docs/development/team-performance.md` ("JSONL `zstd` remains the production default.").
- **Evidence:** `grep -rn "zstd" packages/*/src` returns nothing in this repo; `DSH_BENCH_SESSION_COMPRESSION` defaults to `zstd` only inside the benchmark. The production JSONL default lives in the Harness session-persistence package, not here.
- **Impact:** A maintained doc states behavior outside the code it sits beside; if the harness default ever moves, the doc goes stale silently.
- **Basis:** AGENTS.md "it must not define behavior that the code does not implement"; user rule "code wins over prose".
- **Fix:** Attribute the claim to the Harness (`session-persistence-jsonl`), or drop it from the "Current constraints" list.

- **Impact:** A checked box overstates coverage of a self-declared gap. Not a code defect.
